- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true price deviates from 30-day moving average by >2%, model often fails to revert; apply mean reversion correction: forecast = MA ± 1.5×σ (if deviation > 2σ).
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment swings from 0.67→0.33, reduce forecast slope).
